_about: Pinned hashes and known gate failures. Machine-editable by --rebaseline. History in tests/BASELINE.md. READ THIS BEFORE CHASING A HASH: determinismHash and the smoke tables are CHANGE DETECTORS, not the determinism invariant. The invariant is that the same seed+tick+inputs reproduce bit-identically, and the determinism gate tests that separately (twice-run comparison) -- it keeps passing while these values move. All we require is determinism; new numbers are fine. An intentional change to hashed state (a reaction chance, a material, a sim.* value, a re-baked asset) ALWAYS moves them: run --selftest --rebaseline, commit the new values with the change, and move on. Do not investigate an expected move, do not try to restore the old number, and do not call it a broken sim. Only an UNEXPECTED move is a finding.
_recorded_at: 46b7ec7 2026-08-21, RTX 3060 Ti; last re-recorded 2026-08-25 for the GAS VERTICAL MODEL (buoyancy as a redistributable probability)
_treeAtlas_about: tree-atlas gate. treeAtlasHash is FNV-1a over the uploaded atlas buffer (assets/trees/*.svtree, remapped to engine material ids). It moves when a species is re-baked -- which also moves determinismHash, so this is what names WHICH asset did it instead of leaving a world-hash diff with no cause attached. Re-bake with node scripts/bake_trees.mjs, then --selftest --rebaseline.
_scale_about: scale gate. scaleMetres_<def> is that asset's size in METRES, recorded at 10 voxels/metre. These are the cross-scale pins: they are checked against a DIFFERENT kVoxelMeters than they were recorded at, which is the only thing that makes them non-circular (worldSize/skinScale*kVoxelMeters reduces algebraically to box/artVoxelsPerMetre and would agree with itself at any scale). Tolerance is 1.5 cells, since art is quantised and two scales may legitimately land on different whole cells. A move here means an asset changed physical size -- re-author or re-pin deliberately, do not rebaseline reflexively.
_debris_about: KNOWN-FAILING since the tree overhaul (2026-08-29), and the cause is understood: the gate drops 54 rigid bodies into open forest at x 40-125 / z 420-490, and trees now have real branch structure, so bodies get CAUGHT IN CANOPIES instead of reaching the ground. Confirmed by voxel dump -- a 1,752-voxel body hung at y=221 with ground at y=199 and an autumn-birch canopy at y=231. Nothing about the tree code is wrong; the fixture assumed open ground. Two honest fixes are open: make foliage not support rigid bodies (physically right, a behaviour change in src/phys/debris.cpp), or move the drop zone somewhere trees do not grow (cheaper, but then nothing exercises debris landing in a forest).
_waterbody_about: Thresholds for the `waterbody` gate (docs/PLAN_water_master.md M1). The *TolPct and *Max keys are BOUNDS the gate fails against; the gate also records what it MEASURED through --rebaseline (waterbodyVolErrPct, waterbodyAreaErrPct, waterbodyBowlColumnErrPct, waterbodySurfaceSpread, waterbodyAwakeChunks). As of the M1 landing every measured error is EXACTLY 0.00% — the analytic container curve reproduces the authored lake's 2,782,656 eighths and 14,493 surface cells cell for cell, and the parabolic bowl's level-walk matches its column-walk at 128,214 cells on a real r54 tarn. The tolerance is 2% rather than 0 because the WORLD is not obliged to stay that way: pond life replaces water cells with kelp and reeds, and a ruin or a cave could intrude. A non-zero number here is not automatically a bug, but it IS a number that wants explaining before M2's ledger is built on the curve.
_waterbodyM3_about: M3 thresholds (components 6 + 7, the discharge law and the local excite). Pass H punches a 7x7 shaft through the authored lake floor into a sealed 29x29x18 chamber and lets the discharge law drain it for 90 ticks, then settles for 90 more. The identity is boxVoxelEighths + inFlightMpm - debit == boxVoxelEighths(0), and it is NOT a strict equality for either arm: the box contains a churning MPM pool with downstream physics the water-body system does not own (the CA thin-film handling of water sheeting down a shaft, the sun/water evaporation rule, the always-on wake trigger converting CA water beside the jet). Measured at the M3 landing: H1 (excite and splash off) -37 eighths against 35,381 drained and 40,342 in flight, 0.10%; H2 (shipped) -305 against 26,476 drained. `capped` is 0 in both, so the shave was never short and the ledger debited what it granted every tick — the residual is entirely downstream of the ledger. The bounds are assertions that the discharge is not a PUMP, not a claim that a churning pool is lossless.
_waterbodyShell_about: Plan section 9 item 2: the SHELL mitigation for component 7 was UNMEASURED in the design. At sim.drainExciteRadius 6 the shell converted 14,468 cells CUMULATIVELY over the 90-tick window (161/tick), against a solid ball at the r~25 a real vortex implies costing ~33,000 particles at once versus a ~40,000 largest-measured scene. The standing size is what sim.fluidExciteCeiling bounds (8,000); this is the flow through it. The 20,000 bound catches a radius change that reintroduces the ball.
_waterbodyDrainExcite_about: Plan section 9 item 1, REOPENED at M3. M2 measured the surface shave producing 0 excite candidates against 10.9 M cells inspected — the mechanism was not there, because the shave removes from the TOP. A real JET at a real throat is a different question, and the answer is that the mechanism IS there: 51,346 candidates over 90 draining ticks (570.5/tick) against 5,897,839 cells seen, which is the same order as WP5 own 169,616 over 400 ticks (424/tick) on worldlake. It is BOUNDED rather than absent — sim.fluidExciteCeiling and sim.fluidExciteRate are what hold it, and refusal is graceful because refused water is still settled water. The 3,000/tick bound is ~5x the measured value: it catches a regression into an unbounded burst without failing on the normal case.
_caSlopeHybrid_about: ca-slope-hybrid is the ONE gate here left red on purpose, because what it reports is a behaviour and not a stale expectation. Same script as `ca-slope` but at the SHIPPED sim.fluidExciteMode 1, so the CA and the MPM solver both move the water. Measured 2026-08-29: 768 eighths poured down a stepped ramp, 79.4% reach the catch basin against the 90% the CA-only arm clears. Everything else about the run is clean -- mass is EXACT to the eighth, the ledger never parts company, all 12 structure chunks are asleep from tick 100. What is missing is 24 eighths perched on the deck as voxels and 134 eighths carried by 134 live MPM particles that are not in the basin. Those particles are PERMANENT, not slow: the live count by quarter of the run is 134/134/134/134, dead-flat, and over the whole run 1342 excited -> 1342 emitted with 1208 settled and 1208 dead, so settling is the only way a particle dies and these 134 have stopped settling. The mechanism is WP3's settle veto refusing to convert perched water (correctly -- it would create a floating puddle) combined with nothing moving it downhill, so the water parks on the slope in particle form. That is the gate's founding complaint ("on a hill it'll clump and settle on the hill instead of flowing down") coming back in a different representation, plus a per-tick solver cost that never goes away, which is rule 2. Do not rebaseline this to 79.4%: the number is the report, not the bug.
_perf_about: Budgets for the advisory `perf` gate, moved out of C++ literals (they were 8.0 and 16.0 in selftest_sim.cpp) so retuning them costs a JSON edit rather than a rebuild — CLAUDE.md's own rule, which this gate was the last one violating. They were written at a smaller kVoxelMeters and have been unreachable since it changed, so the gate sat red in this file for months asserting an aspiration instead of detecting a regression; a permanently-red advisory gate trains everyone to skip the line. Measured on the reference machine (RTX 3060 Ti, 2026-08-29): sim 10.11 ms/tick on the deliberately-active benchmark scene (explosions and particles every tick, against a 33 ms tick budget at 30 Hz) and 21.37 ms/frame for the best of the four 1080p render passes. The bounds below are those numbers with ~30% headroom, which is a regression detector: a change that makes the sim or the raymarch a third slower fails here. They are NOT a target — if the numbers get better, tighten them.
_fluidReact_about: The `fluid-react` gate used to assert `standing + live + consumed == placed` exactly, and it came up 37 of 2704 eighths short (1.4%) every run, deterministically. That is not a leak: FA_CONSUMED counts eighths eaten off EXCITED fluid, but the authored rule {self: plant, neighbor: water, neighborBecomes: plant} also runs in the CA on SETTLED water voxels, and nothing counts those. The missing water is standing in the world as the new plant cells the gate itself counts and calls a pass. The gate now asserts the properties that survive that: no water is created, the gap never exceeds 8 eighths per plant that grew, and the gap stays under this fraction. 3% against 1.37% measured is ~2x headroom — enough that a plant bed of a different size does not fail it, tight enough that water vanishing with nothing to show for it still does.
_bodies_about: debris and settle-back were carried as KNOWN-FAILING from the terrain scale pass with a documented cause -- BuildTerrainPatches waking every body within 24 voxels faster than SettleBodies' 60-consecutive-inactive-tick countdown. THAT CAUSE WAS WRONG, and finding out cost one run once the reporter recorded the wake at the point it happens instead of leaving a bare count (CLAUDE.md rule 6). Measured 2026-08-29: some body managed a 208-tick quiet run against the 60 a settle needs, and the last terrain wake landed 120 ticks before the end. The wake path is innocent. The two gates had two unrelated causes and neither was shared. settle-back: the 3x3x3 block was dropped onto raw procedural terrain at (80,80), which the terrain overhaul turned into a slope; it rolled 13 voxels downhill and came to rest at an angle more than 20 deg off axis, where SettleBodies deliberately refuses to resample it (PLAN B6, `kAlignCos`). Body high water was 1, so nothing else ever existed -- the block simply never qualified, and the refusal was correct. The gate now builds its own flat pad, because the shape of worldgen at one hardcoded (x,z) was never its subject. debris: ONE 21-voxel piece of ejecta, thrown clear of the 3x3x3 CPU mirror by the 500-strength blast, ended at (52.8,111.0,212.4) -- 110 voxels under the ground at y=221. ManageTerrain can only build collision for a chunk the cache already holds, PostStep only despawns bodies that leave the 512-voxel residency window, and between those two boundaries a body is simulated with no ground under it: it tunnels into the rock and then never sleeps because the solver keeps depenetrating it. That IS a real defect, it is a physics/streaming design call rather than a test fix, and it is now bounded by debris.buriedMax below instead of hiding inside a red gate. The gate itself asserts the thing it was written for -- every body still ABOVE ground settles -- and goes red if the buried count grows.
_debris_buried_about: How many debris bodies may end a `debris` run buried below local terrain. 1 is what the gate's blast currently produces (see _bodies_about). This is a KNOWN DEFECT held under a bound, not a tolerance anyone wants: the right value is 0, and it gets there when a body whose surrounding chunks are not cached yet stops being integrated against terrain that does not exist. Raising this number is not a fix.
_mobBurn_about: Floor on how much of the player's FLESH a 90-tick immersion in fire must drive past the sear (flesh_charred + flesh_cinder as a percentage of all flesh). The subtest it guards used to count flesh_cooked as 'charred', so a body that only seared scored the same as one that burned -- which is how 'the player only blackens along the outlines of its limbs' sat under a green gate. Measured 9.8% before the world-pitch neighbour reading in MobSystem::BurnOneLimb and 23.7% after; the floor sits between them.
_terrain_about: Thresholds and measurements for the `terrain` gate. The *Max/*Slack/*Margin keys are BOUNDS the gate fails against and are hand-tuned; the *Observed keys are what the last run measured and are written by --rebaseline. Retuning a bound is a JSON edit, not a rebuild.
_smoke_about: Pinned hash sequences for --vk-smoke and --vk-smoke-loud. Each entry is [tick, hash]. tick 0 = worldgen. Re-record with --rebaseline.
